clue.text: Suspicious of seafood

definitions.meaning: something dubious or questionable smells off
relating to or tasting of creatures caught in the sea

explanation.surface: Someone eyeing a plate of prawns with deep distrust.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: informal dubiousness, as in a dodgy story, and the literal sense of being like or about fish.

clue.text: Husband goes to ground in his home, symbolically

parts.note: earth is soil or ground

explanation.surface: A husband retreats and hides away in his own house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes to ground' suggests hiding, but it only joins H to EARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireside is the traditional emblem of the family dwelling, so it stands for domestic life.

clue.text: How disgraceful that RAF homes have been demolished!

indicators.note: buildings knocked down and rebuilt, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An outraged exclamation that air force housing has been knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have been demolished' rearranges the letters of RAF HOMES. The RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of reproach used when someone behaves badly, meaning the conduct is shameful.

clue.text: Looks for compliments in a letter

definitions.meaning: considers or gazes at, as a verb
good wishes sent at the close of correspondence

explanation.surface: Someone scanning a letter for flattering remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard is to look at something; 'kind regards' are the friendly greetings ending a note.

clue.text: Metal producers put explosive in food containers

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, the explosive going within the containers

parts.note: tins are cans holding food
a mine is a buried explosive device

explanation.surface: Someone planting a bomb inside tins of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Metal producers' looks like smelters or foundries, but it means pits where the ore is dug.
explanation.definitionFit: Pits from which an ore is extracted yield a soft grey element, so they produce it.

clue.text: Steal bedspread to get shelter

parts.note: to take is to steal
a cover is a bedspread or quilt

explanation.surface: A thief pinches a quilt to keep warm and protected.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to find protection from danger, such as gunfire or rain.

clue.text: All the ammunition needed to discharge quiet debtor

parts.note: to fire a gun is to discharge it
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
an ower is one who owes money

explanation.surface: Someone needs every bullet to shoot a silent person who owes them money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharge' looks like a release from debt, but it means shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: The total capacity of weapons a force can bring to bear is measured by its munitions.

clue.text: Fibre is consumed by Sarah

indicators.note: something eaten ends up inside the eater, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Sal is a pet form of the name Sarah

explanation.surface: Sarah eats something rough and stringy.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong plant strand from agave leaves, used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Second son of Noah was a phoney

parts.note: Ham was one of Noah's three sons in Genesis

explanation.surface: A claim that Noah's second boy was an impostor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second son' reads as Ham's birth order, but 'Second' only gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender or fraud is a fake, someone not what they claim.

clue.text: Home-help clearly has children with exceptional appeal

parts.note: a char is a cleaning woman, a British term for domestic help
read cryptically: the cleaner evidently is a mother, IS MA

explanation.surface: A cleaner who obviously has kids and a magnetic personality.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHAR (charwoman) is a British cleaner; someone who plainly has children IS a MA, so the char is a ma.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnetic personal charm that draws people in is a rare attractiveness.

clue.text: Salt pork for every basket of food

parts.note: ham is cured, salted pork
per means for each

explanation.surface: Salted meat is packed for each picnic basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicker hamper is a lidded container packed with provisions, often a Christmas gift.

clue.text: Stop to find a small house in Western Australia

indicators.note: the house is placed inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: WA is the abbreviation for the state of Western Australia
HO is the abbreviation of house

explanation.surface: Someone halts to look for a cottage in Perth's state.
explanation.definitionFit: A command used to halt a horse, so a call to stop.

clue.text: Act by obsequious agent to gain control

parts.note: to do is to act
a minion is a servile follower

explanation.surface: A fawning underling acts to seize power.
explanation.definitionFit: Sovereign authority or rule over a territory is power exercised over it.

clue.text: Had barely enough time to get minced meat

definitions.meaning: allowed only a very narrow margin before a deadline

explanation.surface: A cook in a rush only just manages to prepare the mince.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means left a tiny margin of time; literally, chopped something small, as a butcher does with meat.

clue.text: Politician engulfed by regulations develops wrinkles

indicators.note: swallowed up inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: rules are regulations
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP buried in red tape starts to look careworn and lined.
explanation.definitionFit: To crease or crumple something, like bedclothes or hair, is a verb of disordering.

clue.text: The French pray to hold boy in gaol

indicators.note: one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: prier is the French verb to pray
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A French phrase-book line: to pray for a lad behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French pray' asks for French: PRIER, which holds SON. 'in gaol' defines one held there.
explanation.definitionFit: A person held in jail is a captive, so the phrase describes the inmate.

clue.text: Disconcerted by finding cigarette remains in a bed

indicators.note: the remains are placed inside the bed phrase

parts.note: abed means in bed
ash is what is left of a smoked cigarette

explanation.surface: Someone is unsettled to find cigarette ash in the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Embarrassed and put out of countenance, as when one feels ashamed.

clue.text: Main struggle to find the vestige of a python

parts.note: a boa is a large constrictor snake, standing in loosely for a python
a trace is a vestige or remnant

explanation.surface: A fight to the finish to find what remains of a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea, not 'chief': the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing race on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing contest on water; the main is a poetic word for the sea.

clue.text: Opposed to changing constitution of the soil

indicators.note: the make-up of the words is altered, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone resists altering the composition of the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Antagonistic and unfriendly towards something, as an enemy is.

clue.text: Philip utterly in love with a southeastern Asian

indicators.note: uttered means spoken, so the name is written as it sounds

parts.note: the name Philip spoken gives the sound FILIP
O is zero, love in tennis

explanation.surface: Philip is completely besotted with someone from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utterly' looks like 'totally' but signals the sound of the name. Love is O, the nil score in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Philippines, an island nation in that region.

clue.text: I have to move back a tiny bit

indicators.note: the word to is turned round, moving back to front

explanation.surface: A request to step backwards just a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I have to' reads as obligation; 'have' merely links, and only the little word 'to' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek letter, the smallest, used to mean a minute amount.

clue.text: Too immersed in professional soldiering

indicators.note: plunged within the words, so the letters are found inside them

explanation.surface: Someone deeply involved in a military career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'immersed in' finds the letters across 'professionAL SOldiering'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean in addition, as well.

clue.text: Emotional saga about a Frenchman

indicators.note: going around, so the saga surrounds the Frenchman

parts.note: a story is a saga
M is the abbreviation of Monsieur

explanation.surface: A dramatic tale centred on a man from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Passionate and tempestuous, like a turbulent relationship.

clue.text: Dam'd strange

parts.note: read as a dam with 'd attached, an archaic contraction, the clue spells out a word for odd

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned oath: damned odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dam'd' looks like 'damned', but a dam is a weir, and adding 'd gives a word meaning strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd and uncanny, out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Buoyed up when given a plastering trowel

parts.note: a float is a flat tool for smoothing plaster

explanation.surface: Someone cheered up when handed a builder's tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buoyed up' might mean cheered, but it means kept on the water's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Supported on water and not sinking.

clue.text: Labour movement needs to shift position

definitions.meaning: the rate at which staff leave and join a workforce

explanation.surface: Trade unions must change their policy stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour movement' suggests the political left, but it is staff coming and going.
explanation.definitionFit: Staff churn is the coming and going of workers; to roll over in bed is to change one's posture.

clue.text: Express contempt for prophet without a name

indicators.note: in the older sense of outside, so the prophet surrounds the name

parts.note: a seer is a prophet

explanation.surface: Someone scorns a prophet who goes unnamed.
explanation.definitionFit: To curl the lip in scorn is a disdainful look or remark.

clue.text: No credit given for illicit German currency

parts.note: black as in black market, illegal
the mark was Germany's currency before the euro

explanation.surface: No praise is due for dealing in illegal Deutschmarks.
explanation.definitionFit: A note of disgrace on a record, the opposite of praise.
